summary: A Travel + Leisure tips article by Stacey Leasca, published April 21, 2022, explains the car's air recirculation button and how to use it. The button cuts off outside air so the AC cools already-chilled cabin air, which speeds cooling in heat waves and can save fuel. The article also warns that the button should be avoided in winter because it traps moisture and can fog windows.
one_line: A 2022 Travel + Leisure tip explaining when to use a car's air recirculation button to cool the cabin faster, save gas, and avoid winter fogging.
key_facts: The article was written by Stacey Leasca and published on April 21, 2022 by Travel + Leisure.
The air recirculation button is usually marked with an icon of a car with a sideways U-shaped arrow inside it.
Eden Tyers & Servicing said the air recirculation button 'effectively cuts off the outside air to the inside of the car'.
According to Eden Tyers & Servicing, the button helps boost AC to make the cabin cold as quickly as possible and stops pollution and exhaust fumes.
The Eden Tyers & Servicing post said the button can reduce pollen for drivers who suffer from hay fever.
The Eden Tyers & Servicing post said the button can stop strong outdoor odors from entering the car.
Without the recirculation button, the car must pull in outside air and work much harder to cool it, according to the article.
The Wall Street Journal reported that cars are typically more fuel-efficient when the air conditioner is set to recirculate interior air.
The Wall Street Journal also noted that 'turning off the air conditioner saves even more fuel.'
The article says the button should be avoided in winter because it traps moisture inside the car, which can cause foggy windows and windshield.
Eden Tyers & Servicing advised that in winter, the 'fresh air' mode is best because it forces outside air through the heater core to warm it before it reaches the driver.
The article states that using recirculation helps the AC system last longer by reducing its workload.
